repositories.readmeExcerpt:
GraphBuff logo
## Graph database engine written in Rust and queried with **Cypher**.

- **Storage:** in memory, hybrid (in-memory graph with a write-ahead log and snapshots) or
  disk-resident paged storage for graphs larger than RAM
- **Cypher:** query planner, streaming execution, indexes, constraints, transactions
- **Protocols:** HTTP/JSON and Bolt (Neo4j drivers), user accounts, TLS
- **Tools:** interactive shell, bulk CSV import, online backup, restore and consistency check
- **GPU:** graph kernels and algorithms on wgpu (Vulkan, Direct3D 12, Metal)

## Quick start

Without a Rust toolchain, start the server with the movies demo graph loaded:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:7475:7475 -p 127.0.0.1:7687:7687 ghcr.io/janvencl/graphbuff --demo movies
```

HTTP/JSON is then on `http://127.0.0.1:7475` and Bolt on `bolt://127.0.0.1:7687`; see
[Install without Rust](#install-without-rust) for prebuilt binaries and
[Data directory and logs](#data-directory-and-logs) for where the server keeps your data.

From source:

```bash
cargo run --release -p graphbuff-cli                               # interactive shell
cargo run --release -p graphbuff-cli -- -i examples/movies.cypher  # load a script, then stay interactive
cargo run --release -p graphbuff-cli -- --data ./data              # durable databases in ./data
cargo run --release -p graphbuff-cli -- --data ./data --persistent # ... in disk-resident storage
cargo run --release -p graphbuff-cli -- --demo movies              # shell with the built-in movies graph
cargo run --release -p graphbuff-server                            # HTTP/JSON server on 127.0.0.1:7475, durable
cargo run --release -p graphbuff-server -- --demo movies           # ... with the built-in movies graph
cargo run --release -p graphbuff-server -- --bolt 127.0.0.1:7687   # ... plus Bolt for Neo4j drivers
cargo test --workspace
```

As a library:

```rust
use graphbuff::{Database, params};

let db = Database::in_memory();
db.execute("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ann'})-[:KNOWS]->(:Person {name: 'Bob'})")?;
let r = db.execute_with_params(
    "MATCH (a:Person {name: $name})-[:KNOWS]->(b) RETURN b.name AS friend",
    &params! { "name" => "Ann" },
)?;
println!("{}", r.to_table());
```

## Install without Rust

### Docker

```bash
docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:7475:7475 -p 127.0.0.1:7687:7687 ghcr.io/janvencl/graphbuff --demo movies
```

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7475/query -H 'Content-Type: application/json'      -d '{"query": "MATCH (p:Person)-[:ACTED_IN]->(m:Movie) RETURN p.name, m.title"}'
```

The image `ghcr.io/janvencl/graphbuff` (tags: `latest` and each version, such as `0.1.0`;
linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) runs `graphbuff-server --bind 0.0.0.0:7475 --bolt 0.0.0.0:7687`
as an unprivileged user, with its databases in the volume `/data` and its log on standard
error (`docker logs`); anything after the image name is added to that command line.
`--demo movies` loads the graph of [examples/movies.cypher](examples/movies.cypher), which
is compiled into the binary, into the default database (unless it already holds data).

Inside the container the server has to listen on every interface, so it warns that it has
no `--token`. Who can reach it is decided by `-p`: `-p 127.0.0.1:7475:7475` publishes the
port to this machine only, which is what makes the command above safe. To publish it to
other machines (`-p 7475:7475`), set a token or user accounts:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 7475:7475 -p 7687:7687 -e GRAPHBUFF_TOKEN=s3cret ghcr.io/janvencl/graphbuff
```

Name the volume to keep the databases when the container is removed (`--rm` above drops
them with the container):

```bash
docker run -d --name graphbuff -p 127.0.0.1:7475:7475 -p 127.0.0.1:7687:7687 \
       -v graphbuff-data:/data ghcr.io/janvencl/graphbuff
docker logs -f graphbuff                        # start-up, failed logins, errors
docker exec -it graphbuff graphbuff --help      # the shell binary is in the image too
```

Add `--slow-query 500` to log queries that take 500 ms or more, `--in-memory` for a
throwaway server, or `-e GRAPHBUFF_LOG_DIR=/data/logs` to write log files into the volume.

Build the image yourself with `docker build -t graphbuff .`.

### Prebuilt binaries

Each [release](https://github.com/JanVencl/graphbuff/releases) carries one archive per
platform, with `graphbuff` (shell) and `graphbuff-server` inside a folder
`graphbuff-VERSION-PLATFORM/`:

| Platform | Archive |
|----------|---------|
| Linux x86-64 (static, any distribution) | `graphbuff-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| macOS Apple silicon | `graphbuff-macos-arm64.tar.gz` |
| macOS Intel | `graphbuff-macos-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| Windows x86-64 | `graphbuff-windows-x86_64.zip` |

and `SHA256SUMS` with the checksums of all four. The file names carry no version, so
`https://github.com/JanVencl/graphbuff/releases/latest/download/graphbuff-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`
always points at the newest release (a specific one: `.../releases/download/v0.1.0/...`).

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/JanVencl/graphbuff/releases/latest/download/graphbuff-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar -xzf graphbuff-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
./graphbuff-*/graphbuff-server --demo movies    # http://127.0.0.1:7475
```

The binaries are plain builds: no `gpu` and no `tls` feature. Releases are cut by pushing a
tag `vX.Y.Z` that matches the workspace version ([release.yml](.github/workflows/release.yml)).

## Storage modes

Each database chooses its storage when it is opened:

```rust
use graphbuff::{Database, HybridOptions, PersistentOptions, StorageMode, SyncPolicy};

let mem = Database::open(StorageMode::InMemory)?;              // volatile
let dur = Database::open(StorageMode::hybrid("data/movies"))?; // durable, fits in RAM
let fast = Database::open(StorageMode::Hybrid(
    HybridOptions::new("data/events")
        .sync(SyncPolicy::OsBuffered)          // no fsync per commit
        .checkpoint_after_bytes(16  `. When the mode is known at compile time,
`Database::with_store(HybridGraph::open(opts)?)` avoids the dynamic dispatch.

| | `Hybrid` | `Persistent` |
|---|---|---|
| Memory use | the whole graph | the page cache (`cache_bytes`, default 64 MiB) plus small metadata |
| Open time | load snapshot + replay log | read metadata (+ replay log after a crash) |
| Reads | `MemoryGraph` speed | cached pages at memory speed, misses read 8 KiB pages from disk |
| Log record per commit | logical operations (small) | full images of the changed pages (larger) |

**Hybrid storage** (`crates/core/src/hybrid.rs`) keeps a `MemoryGraph` and logs every
committed transaction as one checksummed record of logical operations. With
`SyncPolicy::EveryCommit` (the default) a query that returned is durable. A
checkpoint (`db.checkpoint()`, `:checkpoint` in the shell, or automatically once the log
passes `checkpoint_after_bytes`) writes a snapshot by temp-file + rename and empties the
log. On open, the snapshot is loaded and the log replayed. A torn last record from a crash
is cut off, and records already covered by the snapshot are skipped. A `LOCK` file keeps a
second process from opening the same directory. If a log write fails and cannot be undone,
the store refuses further writes until it is reopened.

**Persistent storage** (`crates/core/src/persistent.rs`) keeps the graph in paged files:

```
 /nodes.db   fixed 64-byte node records at id * 64: blob pointer, heads/tails of the
                 outgoing and incoming relationship lists, degrees
 /rels.db    fixed 64-byte relationship records: type, endpoints, prev/next in both
                 endpoints' lists (doubly linked, creation order), blob pointer
 /blobs.db   labels and properties, in chains of 128-byte blocks with a free list
 /index.db   B+tree pages: the label index and every property index
 /groups.db  fixed 64-byte relationship groups of dense nodes: type, next group,
                 heads/tails of that type's two lists, degrees, self-loop count
 /meta       id counters, counts, token tables, free lists, index roots (+ CRC)
 /graph.wal  redo log
```

All page access goes through an LRU **page cache** (`persistent/pager.rs`). Pages changed
by the open transaction are pinned and their before-images kept, so rollback is exact and
uncommitted data never reaches a data file. Read queries run on a **snapshot** that shares
the cache: it reads a pinned page's before-image, and the cache keeps the images that
later commits replaced for as long as a snapshot old enough to need them lives. A commit appends the metadata plus the
after-image of every changed page to the redo log as one checksummed record (fsynced per
`SyncPolicy`); afterwards those pages may be evicted and written back at any time, but
never before their log record is on disk. A checkpoint (explicit, after
`checkpoint_after_bytes` of log, and on close) writes back all dirty pages, fsyncs, replaces
`meta` and empties the log. A transaction may change at most `max_transaction_bytes` of
pages (default 1 GiB; it keeps each changed page and its before-image in memory until it
ends). Changing one page more fails the statement with `Error::TransactionTooLarge` and
rolls the transaction back, instead of growing the cache without bound; `0` leaves only
the limit of one log record (about 4 GiB). On open, log records newer than `meta` are re-applied, which also
repairs data pages torn by a crash; a torn last record is ignored.

A node with more than `dense_threshold` relationships (`PersistentOptions::dense_threshold`,
default 50) becomes **dense**: its relationships are regrouped by type and the node record
points to its chain of group records instead. A typed expansion then walks only the
matching groups, and every degree is read from the group records. Stores written by an
earlier version (format v1) open unchanged; their nodes become dense on their next new
relationship, and the next checkpoint writes the v2 metadata.

Property indexes use the same normalization as `MemoryGraph` (`1` and `1.0` share an
entry). Index keys start with a part that sorts like the value: numbers as `f64`, strings
by their first 128 bytes. That is what range and `STARTS WITH` seeks scan. The exact
value follows; values whose encoding exceeds 256 bytes are indexed by a prefix plus
checksum, and seeks re-check those candidates. The metadata keeps each index's entry
and distinct-value counts (format v4), which the planner's estimates use. Stores from
before format v4 (unsorted keys, or no counts) rebuild their indexes once when opened, in
a single transaction.

## Multiple databases

A `DatabaseManager` holds several named databases, each with its own storage. Clients
use it through a `Session`, which has a current database and runs the database commands:

```cypher
CREATE DATABASE movies;                                   // default storage of the manager
CREATE DATABASE scratch IF NOT EXISTS OPTIONS {storage: 'memory'};
CREATE OR REPLACE DATABASE events
  OPTIONS {storage: 'hybrid', sync: 'os', checkpointAfterBytes: 16777216};
SHOW DATABASES;            // name, storage, default, current, nodes, relationships
SHOW DATABASE movies;
SHOW DEFAULT DATABASE;
USE movies;                               // switch the session's current database
USE scratch MATCH (n) RETURN count(n);    // run one query elsewhere, without switching
DROP DATABASE scratch IF EXISTS;
```

```rust
use graphbuff::DatabaseManager;

let mgr = DatabaseManager::open("data")?;   // or DatabaseManager::in_memory()
let mut s = mgr.session();                  // starts on the default database, `graphbuff`
s.execute("CREATE OR REPLACE DATABASE movies")?;
s.execute("USE movies")?;
s.execute("CREATE (:Movie {title: 'Heat'})")?;
```

* **`CREATE OR REPLACE DATABASE`** drops an existing database with all its data and
  creates it again empty, with the given options; if it doesn't exist it is just created.
  It cannot be combined with `IF NOT EXISTS`. Plain `CREATE DATABASE` fails if the name is
  taken; `IF NOT EXISTS` leaves the existing database alone

## 项目简介

**柠檬跨境ERP（Lemon Ecom ERP）是一套开源、可私有化部署的跨境电商 ERP。** 从选品开发、1688 采购、头程发货、刊登定价，到多平台订单处理、FBA 与海外仓、广告、售后、平台结算和利润核算，跨境卖家每天要做的事在一套系统里完成。与常见的按店铺数、订单量收费的 SaaS ERP 不同，柠檬跨境ERP 全部源码开放，不限店铺、账号和订单量，数据保存在你自己的服务器上。

      11  电商平台连接器
      3 + 3  海外仓 / 物流商对接
      业财一体  订单到凭证自动生成
      19 × 12  自动化触发事件 × 动作
      5  国产大模型可选
      0 元  不限店铺与订单量

### 卖家的难题，我们这样解决

| 你遇到的问题 | 柠檬跨境ERP 的做法 |
| --- | --- |
| 店铺开了十几个，每天在各平台后台来回切换处理订单？ | 11 个平台统一授权、自动拉单、回传发货和库存；审单规则自动分仓、选物流、打标签、挂起风险订单，批量取号打面单、扫描发货 |
| 每月看着流水在涨，算下来却不知道赚没赚钱？ | 结算报告回写真实佣金和配送费，仓储费、广告费、头程、VAT 分摊到订单和 SKU；订单口径与结算口径两套利润报表，全部折算本位币 |
| FBA 一断货排名就掉，一压货仓储费就涨？ | 按加权日均销量与在途库存算补货建议，FBA 库存健康展示超龄、冗余库存和预估仓储费并给出处理建议；头程货件即在途调拨，到货自动入平台仓 |
| 广告越投越多，ACoS 一直降不下来？ | Amazon Ads 数据按活动 / 搜索词 / SKU 拆到 TACOS，广告规则自动调竞价、否词，分时策略按时段调价 |
| 财务月底对账要对一周，平台回款和应收对不上？ | 订单出库即生成成本和应收，结算报告生成收款单核销应收，PingPong、连连、Payoneer 到账流水自动匹配并处理汇兑差额 |
| 运营人多了，权限和业绩说不清？ | 运营只看负责和被授权的店铺，按店铺的数据权限覆盖订单、商品、广告、利润；运营目标与绩效按人按店考核 |
| 重复工作太多，人一直在盯后台？ | 自动化规则中心内置「1 星差评自动建售后工单」「可售天数低于 15 天自动生成采购计划」「预估亏损订单自动挂起」「ACOS 过高暂停活动」「被跟卖立即通知负责人」等模板；AI 运营日报每天推送到钉钉 / 企业微信 / 飞书 |

### 覆盖跨境卖家的全流程

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[产品开发] --> B[1688 / 供应商采购] --> C[本地仓入库] --> D[头程发货]
  D --> E[FBA / 海外仓]
  A --> F[刊登定价] --> G[多平台订单]
  E --> G
  C --> G
  G --> H[打单发货] --> I[售后客服]
  G --> J[平台结算] --> K[回款对账] --> L[利润与凭证]
  M[广告] --> L
```

### 为什么选择柠檬跨境ERP

- **真正开源，没有收费版**：仓库里就是全部功能，没有授权码和功能阉割，不按店铺、账号、订单量收费；GPL-3.0 协议，可以免费商用
- **数据在自己手里**：私有化部署在自己的服务器或云主机上，店铺授权、订单、利润等经营数据不经过任何第三方
- **业财一体，不只是订单工具**：底层是一套完整 ERP，平台订单、采购、调拨都生成真实的库存流水、成本和会计凭证，利润和财务报表口径一致，不需要再导出到另一套财务软件
- **AI 与自动化**：AI 问数直接问「上个月哪个店铺利润最高」「哪些 SKU 要紧急补货」；AI 写 Listing 并检查违禁词，草拟买家消息和评价回复；自动化规则把重复操作交给系统
- **可以拿来做 SaaS**：内置多租户、租户套餐和行业模板，服务商可以直接为多家卖家提供在线服务
- **方便二次开发**：Spring Boot 4 + Vue 3，模块单向依赖，新增平台只需实现一个连接器接口；自带完整演示数据、用户手册和开发文档

### 适合谁用

- **中小跨境卖家**：用一台服务器部署，免费管理全部店铺和订单，省下每月的 ERP 订阅费
- **品牌卖家与工贸一体企业**：需要业财一体、审批流、精细化利润和按店铺的权限管理
- **软件服务商与开发者**：以本项目为基础，为客户做部署实施、定制开发或 SaaS 运营

> 如果这个项目对你有帮助，请点一下右上角的 **Star**，这是对我们最大的鼓励！

## 功能总览

按顶部导航的模块：

    模块  主要功能

## 快速开始

### 方式一：免装数据库体验

只需要 JDK 17 和 Node 20+：

```bash
./gradlew bootTestRun                         # 后端：H2 内存库 + 内存缓存
cd lemon-web && npm install && npm run dev    # 前端：http://localhost:5173
```

后端启动完成后会自动生成一套**演示数据**（约 1–2 分钟，看板上显示进度）：一个跨境卖家的 10 个平台店铺（亚马逊美 / 德 / 日、虾皮、TikTok Shop、Temu、速卖通、Shopify、eBay 等）、40 个带图片的商品、供应商与采购、头程货件、近 120 天约 5000 张订单（各作业环节都有）、退货、结算回款、广告、客服、FBA、海外仓、产品开发与 1688 采购、补货与预测。`bootTestRun` 以 SaaS 模式运行，登录时租户填「柠檬科技」；设置 `LEMON_ECOM_DEMO_DATA=false` 可以关闭演示数据。

### 方式二：Docker 一键部署

安装了 Docker（含 Compose v2）时，一条命令启动 MySQL、Redis、后端和前端：

```bash
cd docker
cp .env.example .env        # 修改其中的密码和 JWT_SECRET；需要演示数据时设置 LEMON_ECOM_DEMO_DATA=true
docker compose up -d --build
```

启动完成后访问 http://localhost（端口见 `.env` 中的 `WEB_PORT`）。也可以使用 Release 中的 Docker 部署包，直接拉取 `ghcr.io` 上的镜像。

### 方式三：源码运行（MySQL + Redis）

```bash
# 1. 初始化数据库（会删除并重建全部表）
mysql -uroot -p -e "CREATE DATABASE lemon_ecom DEFAULT CHARSET utf8mb4"
mysql -uroot -p lemon_ecom  /ecom/oauth/callback/ `。详见 [部署文档](https://makesomefakenews.github.io/lemon-ecom-website/dev/deploy/)。

## What it is

CodeForge AI is a self-contained, action-first programming assistant that runs on your own machine. Short calculator, command and code requests return runnable code instead of a long deliberation; deeper reasoning is reserved for tasks that need it. It executes programs in isolated workspaces and **automatically repairs failing code** by combining compiler diagnostics with a large language model. Models are downloaded as GGUF files and served locally by `llama.cpp`.

Local inference stays on the machine. When you configure an **online brain** (any DeepSeek-compatible OpenAI API) and the device is connected, the router sends that request to the online model for maximum capability; if the network or the API fails, the request automatically falls back to the local model. Everything learned online — answers, web snippets and research findings — is written into a persistent local memory store, so the offline brain keeps the knowledge after the connection drops.

**Core capabilities**

- **Action-first replies** — simple calculator, command and code requests return executable code in seconds instead of disappearing into a long monologue. The managed runtime caps reasoning with `--reasoning off --reasoning-budget 256` and disables the chat template's thinking mode; the model still reasons when the task genuinely needs it. A capped-reasoning calculator request returned code in 4.6 s.
- **Dual-brain routing** — online DeepSeek-class capability when configured and reachable, local offline inference otherwise, with automatic fallback and `route`/`route_error` reported on every request.
- **Persistent memory** — append-only JSONL memory with CJK bigram + Latin tokenization, SHA-256 deduplication, relevance scoring, kind weights, recency decay and pruning. Chat turns, web findings, debug outcomes and distilled online lessons are recalled offline.
- **Workspace index** — the server indexes project sources (up to 1,500 files, secret/config/build directories excluded) into `memory/project-index.jsonl`, so questions about your own repository are answered with real paths and excerpts.
- **Agentic debug loop** — run → collect diagnostics → ask the model for a patch → re-run, for up to eight iterations (default three), with full process-tree timeouts. RUN, PREVIEW, SAVE and placement work even when no model is running.
- **Multi-language execution** — Python, C, C++, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, PHP and C# are compiled and executed inside per-run workspaces with captured stdout/stderr. Missing runtimes are downloaded on demand from the official sources into `native/toolchains/ `, with live progress and no system PATH changes.
- **HTML/CSS live preview** — generated pages render in a sandboxed iframe served from a per-run session folder with a strict CSP.
- **Model-independent workbench** — compile/run buttons, **AUTO COMPILE**, save-to-any-path, language downloads, project placement and launcher creation are executed by the local server and the LOCAL OPS chat layer. A 4B offline model, a 30B model or an online API all get the same execution and placement capabilities; only the prose differs.
- **Any command, any installed application, any platform** — the Command Agent runs PowerShell, cmd, bash, sh or zsh commands on Windows, macOS and Linux, not only programming tasks. It discovers installed tools and 156 applications on this host, carries per-platform control references for Office/WPS/LibreOffice, browsers, media, archives, OCR, cloud CLIs and databases, and can download 70 missing tools automatically through portable toolchains, the native package manager, pip or npm. If it meets unfamiliar software it searches, reads official documentation and then uses it.
- **Publishing with a guard** — the agent can prepare commits, builds, packages, release assets and site deploys. Public actions (`git push`, release/PR/issue creation, registry/container pushes, remote copies, cloud deploys and write HTTP methods) stay blocked until **Allow publishing** is enabled in the Command Agent settings or the run is started through the API with `allow_publish=true`; blocked calls identify themselves instead of failing silently.
- **Any file, any path** — code blocks can be saved to the exact path you type (one path per file), missing folders are confirmed before creation, and nothing is silently renamed. The whole project can be copied to any folder, any file or folder can be copied or moved to a chosen path, the Desktop, or a bare drive (`D`, `D盘`, `D盘根目录`), and a real launcher can be created anywhere (Windows `.lnk`, Linux `.desktop`, macOS `.command`).
- **12 curated offline models** — a mix of Chinese and international models including Qwen3-Coder, DeepSeek, Seed-OSS, GPT-OSS, Devstral, Gemma, Phi and Codestral.
- **Domestic model downloads** — every offline model resolves through `hf-mirror.com` by default, with automatic `huggingface.co` fallback, resumable transfers and mandatory upstream SHA-256 verification. Override the source with `llm.model_mirror` or `CODEFORGE_MODEL_MIRROR`.
- **CPU or CUDA llama.cpp runtime** — install the managed CPU build (Windows x64/ARM64, macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64/ARM64/s390x, Android ARM64), or add the official CUDA build and let CodeForge detect it. The runtime panel offers **Auto / CPU / CUDA**; Auto uses the GPU build when present, CUDA offloads all 99 layers, and CPU remains the fallback for machines without an NVIDIA GPU. The server verifies SHA-256, retries through GitHub mirror fallbacks when the asset host is blocked, and controls `llama-server` with a user-selectable 2K–512K context window (16K default).
- **Faster answers on NVIDIA hardware** — the CUDA build measured ~83.6 tok/s on an RTX 4070 12 GB versus ~4.5 tok/s on CPU for the same Qwen3 4B model, while a direct `add(a,b)` completion returned code in 0.8 s. Short prompts and cap-limited reasoning reach code quickly instead of deliberating.
- **Adjustable reply limit for every offline model** — one shared 64–393,216-token reply budget, editable in the runtime panel and applied to the next reply without restarting inference; local generation timeouts scale with the requested budget, up to 288 hours (12 days). The model's context window minus the prompt remains the real cap on the actual reply.
- **Native control center** — a Win32 C++ app that starts the server, shows live readiness, and opens the console in an Edge app window.
- **One web console everywhere** — the same responsive futuristic UI works on desktop browsers, Android WebView, and iOS WKWebView.
- **Interruptible chat with a live reasoning trace** — every turn shows stage-by-stage execution (memory recall, workspace scan, live research, context assembly, generation), a live token counter with the measured decoding rate on the local runtime, a remaining-time estimate, and a progress bar. The send key becomes **INTERJECT** while the model is working: press it to stop the answer and send your correction immediately, or **STOP** to cancel with an empty box. Cancellation kills the core process on the server, frees the model, and does not write the aborted turn to memory.

## Architecture

- **C/C++ main core** — all orchestration, compilation, execution, diagnostics, model calls, and the debug loop.
- **Java server** — REST API, download manager with resume, archive extraction, runtime management.
- **Python auxiliary core** — environment bootstrap, portable JDK provisioning, build automation, packaging, and a mock LLM for testing.
- **Mobile thin clients** — Kotlin/WebView and Swift/WKWebView shells that connect to a CodeForge server on the device or LAN.

Deeper dives: [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [API reference](docs/API.md) · [Security model](docs/SECURITY.md).

## Request lifecycle

Every action is a bounded subprocess call with a JSON contract. Chat, debug, model download, runtime installation, and the four-language self-test all pass through the same loopback control plane. Timeouts, size caps, and on-disk state are listed in the diagram; exact request and response examples are in the [API reference](docs/API.md).

## Dual brain, memory and online research

    "backend": "auto",

      "enabled": true,
      "base_url": "https://api.deepseek.com",

    }
  },

  "online": { "enabled": true, "research": "auto", "max_results": 3 }
}
```

MiniMax Code WebUI
 Turn a prompt into something that works. Build, review, and keep iterating in your browser—with MiniMax or your own model.

   Get started  ·
   Documentation  ·
   Features  ·
   Contributing

  English  ·  简体中文

Choose a project folder, describe a task, and follow the agent's work in one browser workspace. Keep the conversation, files, terminal, changes, and previews together as you iterate.

MiniMax Code WebUI home and task composer

  Run it locally →  ·  Configuration and deployment →

**A browser interface with a local runtime.** The server runs on your computer or a machine you manage; the browser connects to that server. Model calls use your MiniMax account or configured provider and may incur charges. This repository is the WebUI fork of [MiniMax Code](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/minimax-code), retaining its TUI, headless CLI, and ACP sources.

## Quick start

### 1. Install the WebUI

Install a supported **Node.js version: 22.19+ (22.x), 24.2+ (24.x), 25, or 26**, then run:

```bash
npm install --global @minimax-webui/minimax-code
mcode-webui
```

With **npm 12 or later**, explicitly allow the native dependency install scripts:

```bash
npm install --global @minimax-webui/minimax-code --allow-scripts=better-sqlite3,bufferutil,node-pty,utf-8-validate
```

The service listens on `http://127.0.0.1:2233/` and opens your default browser when launched in an interactive terminal. If it does not open, use the address printed in the terminal. Keep the process running while you work; press **Ctrl+C** to stop it.

Check the installed command without starting the runtime:

```bash
mcode-webui --version
mcode-webui --help
```

The WebUI has its own npm package and launcher. The upstream CLI installer installs `mcode`; use the command above to install `mcode-webui`.

### 2. Sign in or bring your own model

Open the account menu in the lower-left corner to sign in to MiniMax. An existing CLI login can be reused when both clients use the same data directory. Account models and managed services require the corresponding account access and available quota.

For your own model, open **Settings → Usage & models → Custom models**, add a provider, enter its endpoint and API key, and choose a model. Supported API formats include `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`, and `anthropic-messages`. The model settings also offer the official MiniMax API source.

Model selection lives in the composer. Available models can expose thinking controls and context-window choices:

Model selection, thinking controls, and context-window choices

The default data directory is `~/.minimax`, shared with the CLI. It contains account state, model configuration, and session history. Set `MINIMAX_DATA_DIR` before starting the server to use a separate directory.

### 3. Work in your own project

Click **Select folder**, choose a project on the machine running the server, and describe your task. For example:

> Find a failing test, explain the cause, fix the implementation, and run the relevant tests.

Follow responses and tool activity, review file changes, and use the workspace panels for files, diffs, terminals, and previews. Choose the permission mode in the composer to control how the agent requests approval.

When connecting from another computer, the project folder and terminal belong to the **server's machine**.

### Continue your work

Use the sidebar to reopen projects and conversations, import session bundles, queue follow-up messages, and inspect task progress. Use **Scheduled tasks** to create recurring or one-time work; keep the WebUI runtime running for scheduled execution.

### Connect from another device

The server binds to loopback by default. To make it reachable on your LAN:

**macOS / Linux / WSL**

```bash
WEBUI_HOST=0.0.0.0 WEBUI_OPEN_BROWSER=0 mcode-webui
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
$env:WEBUI_HOST = "0.0.0.0"
$env:WEBUI_OPEN_BROWSER = "0"
mcode-webui
```

Open the printed LAN URL, including its per-start token. When using Mini Apps remotely, the shared Mini App port must also be reachable. See [startup examples and access options](packages/webui/README.md#startup-examples).

The **Remote** page also offers MiniMax App pairing and IM connections, subject to account and service availability:

Remote connection page in MiniMax Code WebUI

## Uninstall

Stop the running WebUI with **Ctrl+C**, then use the same npm installation used to install it:

```bash
npm uninstall --global @minimax-webui/minimax-code
```

Uninstalling leaves the runtime data directory in place. Back up account configuration and sessions before removing data. Check `MINIMAX_DATA_DIR` and whether another CLI or WebUI installation shares the directory before deleting anything.

## What you can do

| Task | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| **Edit and verify code** | Ask the agent to inspect projects, edit files, run commands and tests, and present changes for review. |
| **Review work in context** | Keep files, diffs, terminal sessions, rendered documents, and previews beside the conversation. |
| **Choose your model** | Use MiniMax account models, the official MiniMax API, custom compatible providers, and supported OAuth providers. Adjust the controls each model exposes. |
| **Extend the workspace** | Install and manage plugins, Skills, MCP servers, and browser-capable Mini Apps. |
| **Use the browser** | Configure Browser Use with isolated Chromium or a paired Chrome/Edge extension; availability depends on the selected provider and setup. |
| **Keep work moving** | Reopen conversations, use subagents, queue follow-ups, and create scheduled tasks. |
| **Connect remotely** | Access a server-hosted WebUI in your browser, or use the Remote page for supported mobile and IM integrations. |

Plugin and Skill marketplace

Plugins and Mini Apps can depend on platform capabilities, additional setup, or external accounts. Managed search, media, and connector tools require the relevant beta setting, authorization, and service access. See [known gaps and service boundaries](packages/webui/docs/known-gaps.md) for current limits.

## Build from source

You need Git, a supported Node.js version, and **pnpm 9.12.0**. On Windows, keep the checkout on a local NTFS volume outside cloud-synced folders.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mcode-webui/minimax-code.git
cd minimax-code
git switch webui
node scripts/check-windows-source-location.mjs
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build:webui
pnpm --filter @mavis/webui dev:server
```

Open the address printed by the server. It serves the built client on port `2233`. The first build requires network access to download dependencies and build resources.

For client hot reload, keep the runtime service running and start Vite in a second terminal:

```bash
pnpm dev:webui
```

Open `http://localhost:5173/`. See [the WebUI development guide](packages/webui/README.md#run-from-source) for port overrides and local npm package builds.

### Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WEBUI_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Server bind address. |
| `WEBUI_SERVER_PORT` | `2233` | WebUI HTTP and WebSocket port. |
| `WEBUI_MINIAPP_PORT` | `49152` | Shared Mini App HTTP and WebSocket port. |
| `MINIMAX_DATA_DIR` | `~/.minimax` | Account, configuration, and session data. |
| `WEBUI_OPEN_BROWSER` | Open when stdout is a terminal | Set `0` to prevent automatic browser opening. |

The packaged launcher also supports `--full-access`, which disables WebUI token authentication for HTTP, WebSocket, and Mini App services. Anyone who can reach those services can use their WebUI operations. It does not change Agent tool permissions or the bind address. Omit it to retain the default token policy; see [access options](packages/webui/README.md#access-without-a-webui-token).

## Documentation and contributing

- [Install, configure, and run the WebUI](packages/webui/README.md)
- [WebUI architecture and technical documentation](packages/webui/docs/README.md)
- [Contributor guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [WebUI development rules](packages/webui/AGENTS.md)
- [Upstream CLI and shared runtime documentation](docs/README.md)

English is the primary documentation language. The [Chinese README](README_ZH.md) mirrors this page. See the contributor guide for contribution and review requirements.

## Feedback and contact

| Channel | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [WebUI GitHub Issues](https://github.com/mcode-webui/minimax-code/issues) | WebUI bug reports, feature requests, and questions. |
| [Upstream MiniMax Code](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/minimax-code) | Upstream CLI, desktop product information, and the original project. |
| [Security policy](SECURITY.md) | Vulnerability reporting guidance. Keep exploit details and credentials out of public issues. |

For a WebUI bug, include `mcode-webui --version`, your operating system and Node.js version, the installation method, and a minimal reproduction. Remove credentials, account details, and private project content from reports.

## License

First-party code defaults to [MIT](LICENSE). Existing file-level and package-level licenses remain in place. See [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [license status](LICENSE-STATUS.md) for dependencies, assets, and `mcode-tools`.

> 🎓 Part of the free, open-source **AI Career Curriculum** ecosystem — [Infrastructure](https://github.com/ai-infra-curriculum) · [ML Engineering](https://github.com/ml-engineering-curriculum) · [AI Engineering](https://github.com/ai-engineering-curriculum) · [Governance](https://github.com/ai-governance-curriculum) · [Startup](https://github.com/ai-startup-curriculum) · [Workforce](https://github.com/ai-workforce-curriculum).

Welcome to the **Junior AI Infrastructure Engineer Learning Repository**! This comprehensive curriculum is designed to take you from beginner to job-ready in AI/ML infrastructure, with hands-on projects and industry-relevant skills.

## 🎯 Learning Objectives

By completing this curriculum, you will be able to:

- **Deploy ML models** via REST APIs with Flask/FastAPI
- **Containerize applications** using Docker
- **Orchestrate deployments** on Kubernetes
- **Build ML pipelines** with experiment tracking (MLflow)

- **Deploy to cloud platforms** (AWS/GCP/Azure)
- **Implement CI/CD** for ML applications
- **Apply security best practices** for production systems

# TableMinus

**A fast, native SQL & database workbench built in Rust for Windows.**

[CI](https://github.com/williamcachamwri/TableMinus/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[Release](https://github.com/williamcachamwri/TableMinus/actions/workflows/release.yml)
[Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/)
[GPUI](#why-tableminus-exists)
[Drivers](#supported-engines--connection-security)
[Memory](#real-world-benchmarks)
[Startup](#real-world-benchmarks)
[Windows](#installation--auto-updates)
[License: MIT / AGPL-3.0](LICENSE-MIT)

[English](README.md) · [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Français](README.fr.md)

---

## Overview

TableMinus is a native Windows SQL and database workbench written in Rust. It uses [HeroGPUI](https://github.com/williamcachamwri/TableMinus) over Direct3D 11 for rendering and builds on [TablePro](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro)'s open-source Rust database core, skipping Electron and JVM runtimes altogether.

On Windows 11 release builds, cold startup runs around `10 ms` (measured `9.21` to `10.11 ms` via `--smoke-startup` with all 9 drivers registered), and process memory stays near `~55 MB` during `100k` / `500k` / `1M`-row stress queries. In the `tableminus-e2e` SQLite suite, loading `100k` rows into the grid takes `24.43 ms` and scrolling `10k` frames takes `0.432 ms`.

---

## Screenshots

### SQL editor, live charts, and query results

TableMinus SQL Editor and Live Charts

### Virtualized data grid, column aggregates, and parameterized filters

TableMinus Data Grid view

### Interactive ER Diagram, foreign key relations, and SVG export

TableMinus ER Diagram Workbench

### Import Wizard (CSV, JSON, XLSX) with automatic type mapping

TableMinus Import Wizard

### Schema & Data Compare with diff summary and sync script generation

TableMinus Schema and Data Compare

### Mock Data Generator with deterministic seeds and foreign-key ordering

TableMinus Mock Data Generator

### Cross-Engine Data Transfer with live DDL preview

TableMinus Cross-Engine Data Transfer

### Metadata Search palette (`Ctrl+P` / Object Search)

TableMinus Metadata Search

### Schema-only AI drawer (`Ctrl+Shift+A`)

TableMinus Schema-Aware AI Assistant

---

## Supported Databases

TableMinus compiles 9 database drivers directly into `tableminus.exe`, with no external ODBC setup or runtime plugins required:

| Database | Driver Crate | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PostgreSQL | `tablepro-driver-postgres` | `tokio-postgres` + `deadpool`, `COPY IN`, schema and DDL inspection |
| MySQL / MariaDB | `tablepro-driver-mysql` | Full SQL dialect and catalog metadata |
| SQLite | `tablepro-driver-sqlite` | Local `.sqlite` / `.db` files via file open, drag-and-drop, or CLI |
| DuckDB | `tablepro-driver-duckdb` | Bundled DuckDB 2.0 with `json` and `parquet` linked in |
| Microsoft SQL Server | `tablepro-driver-mssql` | Pure-Rust TDS 8.0 (`tiberius`) with TLS and multi-result batches |
| ClickHouse | `tablepro-driver-clickhouse` | HTTP/TLS queries via `hyper-rustls` |
| Cassandra / ScyllaDB | `tablepro-driver-cassandra` | Native CQL (`scylla`) over `rustls` |
| MongoDB | `tablepro-driver-mongodb` | Document queries, BSON 3 mapping, DNS seed list resolution |
| Redis | `tablepro-driver-redis` | Key-value inspection and command execution over async TLS/TCP |

Connections support in-process SSH tunneling via `russh` (`tablepro-ssh` with password, private key, passphrase prompt, and host-key verification), TLS via `rustls` and the Windows certificate store (`Disable`, `Prefer`, `Require`, `VerifyCA`, `VerifyFull`, plus custom CA and client cert/key files), Safe Mode policies (`Off`, `ConfirmWrites`, `ReadOnly`), and importing saved connections from other database tools via `tablepro-foreign-import`.

---

## Features

### SQL Editor & Data Grid

The editor supports dialect-aware syntax highlighting (`PostgreSQL`, `MySQL`, `SQLite`, `MsSql`, and others), autocomplete for tables, columns, schemas, keywords, and SQL clauses (`FROM`, `JOIN`, `INTO`, `UPDATE`), multi-cursor editing, a saved query library, persistent query history, and optional Vim mode (`NORMAL`, `INSERT`, `VISUAL`, `COMMAND`).

In the data grid, you can inspect rows in a docked Row Inspector (`Ctrl+I`), switch between Structure, Columns, Indexes, Foreign Keys, and DDL tabs, pin leading columns up to 2/3 of the viewport width, resize or hide columns, and stack parameterized filters across 11 operators (`=`, `!=`, `Contains`, `StartsWith`, `EndsWith`, ` `, `>=`, `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL`). Cell edits, inserted rows (`Alt+Insert`), and deleted rows (`Ctrl+Shift+Backspace`) are staged in a batch until you commit (`Ctrl+Shift+S`) or roll back (`Ctrl+Shift+R`).

Query results and tables export atomically through `.part` staging files to CSV (`.csv`), JSON Array (`.json`), JSON Lines (`.jsonl`), or SQL `INSERT` (`.sql`) via `Ctrl+Shift+E`. `tablepro-core` also includes TSV, XML, and constant-memory XLSX encoders.

### Security & Local Storage

Database passwords, SSH secrets, AI API keys, and MCP bearer tokens are stored in Windows Credential Manager (`CredWriteW` / `CredReadW`) and scrubbed from memory with `zeroize` rather than written to plain JSON config files or logs. Connections can be locked to `ConfirmWrites` or `ReadOnly` in Safe Mode so `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, and `DROP` statements either prompt first or fail before execution.

### AI Assistant & MCP Server

The AI drawer (`Ctrl+Shift+A`) connects to local Ollama (`http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`), any OpenAI-compatible server, OpenAI, or Anthropic. Only schema metadata (table names, column names, types, and SQL dialect) is sent to the model; table row data stays local.

For external coding agents and IDEs, `tablepro-mcp` runs a loopback HTTP MCP server on `127.0.0.1` authenticated with a Bearer token in Windows Credential Manager and peer verification. It exposes 11 tools:

- `list_connections`, `connect`, `list_databases`, `list_schemas`, `list_tables`, `describe_table`, `get_table_ddl`, `browse_table`, `count_rows`, `execute_query`, and `export_data`

`execute_query` obeys each connection's External Clients and Safe Mode settings and requires confirmation inside TableMinus before any write query runs.

### Themes, Backdrops & Languages

TableMinus includes 14 built-in themes (`Dark`, `Light`, `High Contrast`, `Gaussian Glass Dark`, `Gaussian Glass Light`, `Tokyo Night`, `Dracula`, `Catppuccin Mocha`, `One Dark Pro`, `Nord`, `Monokai Pro`, `Gruvbox Dark`, `GitHub Light`, and `Catppuccin Latte`). UI themes and syntax palettes can be chosen independently, or you can import a VS Code `.json` color theme.

On Windows 11, the main window supports DWM `Gaussian Blur`, `Mica`, `Mica Alt`, and `Opaque` materials while keeping floating overlays opaque (`1.0` alpha) for readability. Reduced Motion follows Windows `SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION` so drawers and modals skip transitions when system animations are turned off. All UI labels, menus, modals, tooltips, and driver diagnostics are localized in 6 languages: `en-US`, `vi-VN`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`, and `fr-FR`.

### CLI Usage

`tableminus.exe` works as both the desktop launcher and a scriptable CLI (`tablepro-cli`). Passing `.sqlite`, `.db`, `.duckdb`, or `.sql` file paths or connection URLs (`postgresql://...`) opens them in the running instance over Named Pipe IPC (pass `-n` / `--new-window` to open a separate window).

Top-level flags:
- `--version` (`-V`) prints the version and exits.
- `--help` (`-h`) prints CLI usage and options.
- `--smoke-startup` runs a headless startup timing check and verifies all 9 drivers register.

Subcommands: `open`, `query`, `connections`, `databases`, `schemas`, `tables`, `describe`, `export`, `status`, and `completion` (`bash`, `zsh`, `fish`), with `--format`, `--read-only`, `--limit`, and `--timeout` options.

```powershell
# Run a read-only query and print JSON Lines
.\target\release\tableminus.exe query -c Staging --read-only --format jsonl "SELECT id, email FROM users LIMIT 10"

# Print CREATE TABLE DDL for a table
.\target\release\tableminus.exe describe -c Staging --ddl users
```

---

## Download & Install

Requires **Windows 10 or Windows 11 (x64)**. Prebuilt binaries are published on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/williamcachamwri/TableMinus/releases):

- **Installer (`TableMinus-win-Setup.exe`)**: Installs into `%LocalAppData%` with Start Menu and desktop shortcuts without requiring UAC elevation. Uses Velopack for background binary delta updates, configurable in **Settings -> About**.
- **Portable (`TableMinus-win-Portable.zip`)**: Extract to any folder and run `tableminus.exe` directly without modifying installer state.

Each release includes `SHA256SUMS.txt` so you can check downloads in PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\TableMinus-win-Setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```

---

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Ctrl+K` / `Ctrl+Shift+K` / `Ctrl+P` | Open Command Palette |
| `Ctrl+Enter` / `F5` | Run active SQL query |
| `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` | Run selected SQL text |
| `Shift+Esc` | Cancel running query |
| `Ctrl+S` | Save query to library |
| `Ctrl+T` / `Ctrl+W` / `Ctrl+Shift+T` | New query tab / Close tab / Reopen closed tab |
| `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | Next / Previous tab |
| `Ctrl+F` | Focus object sidebar filter |
| `Ctrl+B` | Toggle object sidebar |
| `Ctrl+I` | Toggle Row Inspector |
| `Ctrl+Shift+A` | Toggle AI Assistant drawer |
| `Ctrl+Shift+O` | Open Connections library |
| `Ctrl+,` | Open Settings |
| `Ctrl+Shift+M` | Cycle theme |
| `Ctrl+Shift+S` / `Ctrl+Shift+R` | Commit / Rollback staged grid edits |
| `Alt+Insert` / `Ctrl+Shift+Backspace` | Add row / Delete selected rows in grid |
| `Ctrl+Shift+E` | Export results or table |
| `Esc` | Dismiss active modal or overlay |

Vim navigation (`NORMAL`, `INSERT`, `VISUAL`, and `:` commands) can be enabled from the SQL editor toolbar.

---

## Build from Source

### Prerequisites

- Windows 10 or Windows 11 (x64)
- Stable Rust MSVC toolchain (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, Rust `2024` Edition) via [rustup](https://rustup.rs/)
- Visual Studio C++ Build Tools and Windows SDK (for Win32, Direct3D 11, and bundled C drivers)
- Windows PowerShell (use `;` instead of `&&` to chain commands)

> [!CAUTION]
> Always build and test with `--release`. Avoid running unprofiled debug `cargo build` or `cargo test` across the workspace unless you specifically need debug symbols, as PDB files in `target\debug` for all crates and 9 drivers grow past 140 GB. Pass `-j 1` on memory-constrained machines.

### Build & Test Commands

```powershell
# Make sure an existing tableminus.exe process is not locking target\release\tableminus.exe
Get-Process tableminus -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# Type-check and build the release binary
cargo check --release -j 1 -p tableminus-windows-app
cargo build --release -j 1 -p tableminus-windows-app

# Run the headless startup check and launch the app
.\target\release\tableminus.exe --smoke-startup
.\target\release\tableminus.exe
```

Release test suites:

```powershell
cargo test --release -j 1 -p tablepro-core filter
cargo test --release -j 1 -p tableminus-e2e --test startup_perf_e2e -- --nocapture
cargo test --release -j 1 -p tableminus-e2e --test sqlite_e2e -- --nocapture
```

### Workspace Layout

| Path | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| `core/crates/core` | `tablepro-core`: query models, filters, SQL dialects, export encoders |
| `core/crates/session` | `tablepro-session`: live sessions, connection pools, transactions |
| `core/crates/cli` | `tablepro-cli`: CLI subcommands and headless runner |
| `core/crates/mcp` | `tablepro-mcp`: token-authenticated localhost MCP HTTP server |
| `core/crates/ai` | `tablepro-ai`: schema-only Ollama, OpenAI, and Anthropic client |
| `core/crates/ssh` | `tablepro-ssh`: in-process `russh` SSH tunneling |
| `core/crates/net` | `tablepro-net`: `rustls` TLS and system certificate verification

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
Laravel Database Backup

Back up your Laravel database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB) to a private S3-compatible bucket on a schedule, with email and Discord notifications.

## Why

- **Database only.** Your code lives in Git; this backs up the one thing Git does not have.
- **Streams the dump.** `pg_dump` / `mysqldump` output is gzipped while it streams, so a 1 GB database never sits in memory.
- **Restores, tested.** The test suite dumps a real PostgreSQL and MySQL database, restores the file into an empty one and compares every row.
- **Private by default.** The file is uploaded private, the password never reaches the command line, and notifications never link to the file.
- **Tells you.** Every run, successful or failed, by email and on Discord.

## Requirements

- PHP 8.3+ and Laravel 12 or 13.
- PostgreSQL (`pg_dump`), MySQL or MariaDB (`mysqldump`) on the server that runs the scheduler. `pg_dump` must be the same major version as the server or newer.
- A private S3-compatible bucket: Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO...

## Installation

```bash
composer require paulocastellano/laravel-database-backup
```

Then set your bucket and turn the schedule on in `.env`:

```dotenv
BACKUP_ENABLED=true
BACKUP_INTERVAL_HOURS=6            # every N hours on the hour, UTC (1-24)
BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS=30                # 0 keeps every backup

BACKUP_BUCKET=my-backups           # required
BACKUP_DIRECTORY=my-app            # required: one bucket can hold several apps
BACKUP_ENDPOINT=https:// .r2.cloudflarestorage.com
BACKUP_REGION=auto
BACKUP_ACCESS_KEY_ID=
BACKUP_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=

BACKUP_NOTIFY_EMAIL=ops@example.com
BACKUP_NOTIFY_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...

BACKUP_DB_CONNECTION=              # optional: the connection to dump, else the default one
BACKUP_TIMEOUT=3600                # optional: seconds the dump may take
```

`BACKUP_ENDPOINT` picks the provider; leave it empty for Amazon S3. The scheduler must be running (`php artisan schedule:run` every minute), as for any Laravel scheduled task.

The email goes through your app's mailer (`MAIL_*`). The dump is written to the system temporary directory (`TMPDIR`), readable by its owner only, before it is uploaded and deleted, so that directory needs room for one compressed dump.

## Usage

Back up now, whether or not the schedule is enabled:

```bash
php artisan backup:database
```

Each run:

1. dumps the database (the default connection, or `BACKUP_DB_CONNECTION`) to ` /YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.sql.gz`, named after the UTC time;
2. deletes the backups in `BACKUP_DIRECTORY` older than `BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS`. The directory belongs to the backups alone; the rest of the bucket is never listed;
3. sends the result to `BACKUP_NOTIFY_EMAIL` and the Discord webhook. Either left blank is skipped, and a notification that fails never fails the backup.

A failed run (a missing bucket or directory, a dump error, an upload error) throws `PauloCastellano\DatabaseBackup\Exceptions\DatabaseBackupException` or the filesystem's own exception, exits with an error, is reported like any exception, and is announced by email and on Discord. The email is sent at once, not queued, so you hear about it even when your queue workers are down.

### Restoring a backup

There is no restore command, on purpose: one wrong argument would overwrite production. Download the file from your bucket, restore it into a new database, check it, then point your app at it:

```bash
createdb my_app_restored
gunzip -c 20261113135350.sql.gz | psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 my_app_restored

# MySQL / MariaDB
gunzip -c 20261113135350.sql.gz | mysql my_app_restored
```

## Configuration

Publish the config file to change anything beyond the environment variables:

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag="laravel-database-backup-config"
```

### Customizing the emails

The emails are plain Blade views. Publish them to `resources/views/vendor/laravel-database-backup` and edit them there:

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag="laravel-database-backup-views"
```

## Testing

```bash
composer test
```

The restore test runs only against a real server. Point it at an empty PostgreSQL or MySQL database:

```bash
DB_CONNECTION=pgsql DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT=5432 DB_DATABASE=testing DB_USERNAME=postgres DB_PASSWORD= vendor/bin/pest
```

## Built by Paulo Castellano

Hi, I'm Paulo. I built this package for [TryPost](https://trypost.it), where it backs up the production database every few hours. Follow me for what is coming next.
